coverage.assessment: Three logical bridges are cut: the reason for the historian's 'green with horror', the gloss that sets up the 'continuity snapped' paragraph, and the 'never invented his facts' ground for disclaiming responsibility. The Stallo/Langley and 310 setups survive.

In paragraph 4, 'done it' and 'the negation' lose their antecedents. In revision paragraph 6, 'He recalled' follows a paragraph about science and Pearson with no reference to Adams; the first draft has the same weakness, and it is minor.
There is no dialogue. Quoted speech from Pearson, Haeckel, Poincare, the physicists and Balfour remains correctly attributed.

Two qualifications are lost: the hedge 'As far as one ventured to interpret actual science' (cut in the first draft) and Pearson's 'for these are concepts' clause (cut without an ellipsis). 'If this view was correct' still conditions the conclusion. Dates and the age are consistent.
The narrator's ironic distance and the later-date Balfour aside are intact. The Dynamic Theory is prepared but not disclosed early.
The opening loses its wonder at Gibbs and the confession 'never found out'. The anaphora of 'perpetual' and the eighteenth-century deflation are cut. The main epigrams remain.
The woman's ordered universe no longer stands explicitly against science's raft. 'Man knew it was true because he made it' is cut, which weakens the echo of 'Order was the dream of man'.
All three dependencies are intact at both the local and partner endpoints.

findings.claim: The revision cuts two things the first draft kept: the sentence saying Poincare alone felt the historian's need of unity, and the paragraph explaining that Poincare assumes the alternation of simple and complex that Adams had to surrender. The result is a one-line paragraph, 'green with horror', with no stated cause.
findings.counterevidence: Both contradictory Poincare quotations stay together, as the plan requires, and 'but suddenly he fell on another view' still marks the turn.

evidence.quote: but he seemed to be the only authority in science who felt what a historian felt so strongly--the need of unity in a universe.
assuming that the past showed alternating phases of simple and complex--the precise point that Adams, after fifty years of effort, found himself forced to surrender
He burned to ask whether M. Poincare knew any history
Here at last was a fixed point. History and mathematics agreed. "Considering everything we have made some approach towards unity."
A mathematical paradise of endless displacement promised eternal bliss to the mathematician, but turned the historian green with horror.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'M. Poincare seemed to be the only authority in science who felt ... the need of unity in a universe.' Append to paragraph 11 a clause such as 'since he assumed alternating phases of simple and complex--the precise point that Adams, after fifty years of effort, found himself forced to surrender.'

findings.reader_effect: 'History and mathematics agreed' no longer says what they agreed on. The horror reads as a generic reaction rather than as the irony that the mathematician's paradise is the kinetic gas the 'weary Titan of Unity' fears.
findings.title: Poincare sequence loses its 'need of unity' frame and the reason for the historian's horror

The other is 'Man knew it was true because he made it'.

strengths: All eight protected verbatim lines appear intact and in place, including the one-line pivot 'Suddenly, in 1900, science raised its head and denied.'
The Truth genealogy still climaxes on 'a medium of exchange', and Balfour's dating still lands on 'convenience was truth'.
The pairing of Haeckel's 'religious whisper' with Mach's 'Matter was Motion' is kept, along with their agreement with Pearson.
The ball of vibrating motions 'at the feet of the Virgin at Chartres or of M. Poincare' and the closing 'merge ... or succumb' are preserved.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's argumentative spine. All eight verbatim lines survive, as do the 310/Cross clause, Balfour's dating and the authorized Lucretius lines. Further cuts in this pass, however, remove several hinges that made the argument cohere. These include the reason Poincare's alternation turns the historian green, the gloss on Zeno that prepares 'the continuity snapped', the raft/limpet contrast in the woman's universe, and the grounds for Adams's disclaimer of responsibility. Paragraph 4 also has dangling referents left over from the first draft. None of these is a blocker; each can be fixed with a short restoration.
